el: Citizen of an eligible country. At least 2,800 hours (about two years) of work experience. One-year Masters at an eligible UK university.
dl: Applications opened August 2026 and closed October 2026 for the 2027/28 year. Interviews March to April 2027. Results from mid-June 2027.
note: Tuition, economy travel, visa cost, arrival and departure allowances, and a monthly living allowance.
tip: Write about leadership and networking, not only grades.

el: Citizen of, or refugee in, one of about 40 eligible low- or middle-income Commonwealth countries. Upper second class degree, or lower second plus a postgraduate qualification. Apply through a nominating agency.
dl: The 2027/28 round closed on 20 October 2026. Outcomes by July 2027.
note: Full fees, approved airfare, a stipend of £1,712 a month (£2,000 in London) and a study travel grant.
tip: Explain how your studies will have development impact.

el: Masters students up to age 29 and PhD students up to age 35. Only French higher education institutions can apply for you.
dl: The 2027 call opened October 2026. Deadline for receipt by Campus France is 6 January 2027. Results from 12 April 2027.
note: Monthly allowance, with other benefits. Amounts were not verified.
tip: Ask your target French institution early whether it will nominate you.

el: Non-US citizens living in a participating country. Apply through your home-country Fulbright Commission or the US Embassy. About 4,000 grants a year.
dl: Dates vary by country. Check your national Fulbright Commission.
note: Funding support, J-1 visa sponsorship and a health plan. Amounts vary by country.
tip: Show leadership and a plan to return and contribute.

el: You must also be admitted to a full-time Stanford graduate degree. Bachelor's earned January 2020 or later (2027 cohort). No age or nationality limit stated.
dl: The 2027 cohort deadline was 6 October 2026. Applications for the 2028 cohort open in summer 2027.
note: Up to three years of tuition, a living stipend and an annual travel stipend.
tip: Leadership and purpose matter as much as grades.

el: Research students under 35 eligible for Masters or doctoral admission. Apply through a Japanese embassy or through a university.
dl: Set by your embassy or university. Check their posted window.
note: Tuition exempted, round-trip airfare and a monthly allowance.
tip: Contact your embassy early. The embassy route has its own timeline.

el: Under 40, with a GPA of at least 80%. You and both parents must be non-Korean citizens. Masters is 2 years, doctorate 3 years.
dl: Typically announced in February, applications February to March, results in June.
note: Airfare, Korean language training, tuition and a monthly allowance.
tip: Prepare transcripts and a study plan well before February.

el: Age 18 to 28 on 1 August of the year you enrol. Bachelor's degree required. One-year Master of Global Affairs at Tsinghua University.
dl: Global applicants apply April to September 2027 for the 2028 start. The current window has closed.
note: Fully funded Masters in Beijing.
tip: Leadership and a clear global outlook are what they look for.

el: Nationals of listed countries (for example Afghanistan, Bangladesh, India, Kenya, Pakistan, Uganda), with financial need, for the first year of postgraduate study. Preference for under-30s.
dl: The 2026-27 cycle closed. The next one opens in early 2027.
note: Half grant, half loan. Covers tuition and living costs, not travel.
tip: Show financial need and a plan to give back.

el: Talented, service-minded young people, mainly from Africa, selected by partner universities. No PhD.
dl: No central deadline. Each partner university sets its own.
note: Tuition, accommodation, books, mentoring, counselling, leadership development and return airfare if needed.
tip: Check which universities are partners before you apply.

el: Varies by programme. Many need about two years of professional experience and a strong degree.
dl: Often autumn for the following year. Not verified.
note: Monthly stipend, insurance and travel, for specific eligible programmes.
tip: Pick a programme on the DAAD list first.

el: Strong academic record. Apply to each joint programme directly.
dl: Typically January to February. Not verified.
note: Tuition, living costs and travel.
tip: Apply to several joint programmes. Each has its own essay.

el: Significant work or leadership experience and an application to a Swedish programme. Eligible countries only.
dl: Typically January to February. Not verified.
note: Tuition, living costs and travel.
tip: Show leadership in a field that matters to your country.

el: Mainly research and PhD level. Eligible countries only.
dl: Typically autumn. Not verified.
note: Monthly stipend, tuition exemption and insurance.
tip: Find a Swiss professor willing to supervise you first.

n: Holland Scholarship and university excellence awards
el: Non-EEA students with strong academic records.
dl: Typically December to May. Not verified.
note: A one-off or partial award. Combine with another funder.
tip: Use it as one part of a funding stack.

el: Non-UK students admitted to a Cambridge postgraduate degree.
dl: Linked to Cambridge deadlines. Not verified.
note: Full cost of study at Cambridge.
tip: Apply to Cambridge early. The scholarship is part of the same process.

el: Rhodes has country and region constituencies. Clarendon is for students admitted to Oxford.
dl: Linked to Oxford deadlines. Not verified.
note: Full cost of study at Oxford.
tip: Check your country's Rhodes constituency and application route.

el: Citizens of eligible countries, usually with work experience and a plan to return home.
dl: Typically February to April. Not verified.
note: Tuition, living costs and travel.
tip: Link your study plan to a development priority in your country.

el: International students applying through the CSC or a Chinese university.
dl: Typically January to April. Not verified.
note: Tuition, accommodation and a monthly stipend.
tip: Apply through both your embassy route and the university route if allowed.

el: Several years of relevant work experience in peace or development.
dl: Typically mid-year. Not verified.
note: Full funding at a partner university.
tip: Show a record of service and peace-building work.

el: Departments fund strong applicants with tuition waivers and stipends, mostly for PhD and thesis Masters.
dl: With your application, typically December to January.
note: The main route to funding in the US.
tip: Apply early and contact faculty whose research matches yours.

el: Thesis-based programmes often come with funding. You need a supervisor.
dl: With your application, typically December to January.
note: Tuition support and a stipend through your supervisor or department.
tip: Read two papers by each supervisor and mention them in your email.
